sections.kicker: Prepared for Missandry by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site and your Instagram the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: Missandry has a sharp line. The site does not say it.
sections.keep: The tagline. Wear what you say is a complete brand idea in four words.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things
people meet
first.

pins.what: The best line lives in the bio, not on the site.
pins.why: It says why Missandry and not any other tee brand: the clothes speak for you.
pins.how: Put the line on the first screen and build the page around it.
pins.label: Your bio
pins.cost: The site reads as any apparel shop.

pins.what: The site opens with a label that fits any store.
pins.why: A pastoral tote and a stock heading do not match the loud voice on Instagram.
pins.how: Open with a statement in the same voice as the posts.
pins.label: Your site
pins.cost: A first visit from Instagram feels like a different brand.

pins.quote: AI might be the biggest net negative since patriarchy!
pins.what: Voting, stickers, AI and tanks all share one feed.
pins.why: Each cause is real, and together they blur what Missandry stands for first.
pins.how: Choose the one stance that anchors the brand and let the rest orbit it.
pins.label: Your grid
pins.cost: The position is felt but never summed up, so it cannot be repeated.

sections.intro: You asked for a look at Missandry. I spent some time on your site and your Instagram. Three things stood out, and all three point the same way.

sections.body: It is 20 minutes with me. We go through this page together, on Missandry's own screens, and you leave knowing what to change first.
sections.note: A few short questions first, then you pick a time. You can also just reply to the email.

reference: Supreme, from another category. A voice and a logo are enough.
